questions.q: Why is testing asynchronous Apex (@future, Queueable, Batch) harder than testing synchronous code without special handling?
options: Asynchronous Apex cannot be unit tested under any circumstances
Async code doesn't run immediately — it's enqueued to run later, so a test might finish checking results before the job has actually executed
Asynchronous methods are not allowed to perform DML
Async Apex always requires SeeAllData=true
questions.explain: Async Apex runs later, outside the enqueuing transaction — without special handling, a test method could finish and assert on results before the job ever actually ran.

questions.q: What happens to a Queueable job enqueued with System.enqueueJob between Test.startTest() and Test.stopTest()?
options: It is silently discarded and never runs
It runs in parallel with the rest of the test method
It only runs if Test.isRunningTest() returns true
It runs synchronously, to completion, at the point Test.stopTest() executes
questions.explain: Async work enqueued between startTest and stopTest is held and then run synchronously in full the moment stopTest() executes, before the test method proceeds past that line.

questions.q: A test calls Database.executeBatch(new AccountCleanupBatch()) inside a Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() block, with 50 Account records inserted beforehand. What can the test assume once Test.stopTest() returns?
options: All batches of the job have run to completion, regardless of scope size, so all 50 records should reflect the batch's effects
Only the first batch chunk has processed
The batch job has been scheduled but not yet started
Nothing — batch jobs cannot be tested this way at all
questions.explain: Test.stopTest() runs enqueued batch jobs to completion (all batches) before returning control to the test method, so all 50 records should already reflect the batch job's work.

questions.q: What does Test.isRunningTest() return, and when is it appropriate to use?
options: It returns the number of currently running tests; use it to count test executions
It always returns false inside @isTest methods
It returns true when running inside a test context; it's a last resort for branching around genuinely untestable logic, not a general design pattern
It is required in every test class to enable rollback
questions.explain: Test.isRunningTest() returns true inside a test context. It's meant sparingly, for genuinely untestable edge cases — routinely branching application logic on it means the test isn't exercising the real production code path.

questions.q: Besides forcing async work to run synchronously, what other purpose does Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() serve?
options: It disables all code coverage requirements for the block
It deletes all records inserted before startTest() was called
It automatically mocks any HTTP callouts without needing Test.setMock
It gives the code inside the block a fresh set of governor limits, separate from setup code that ran before startTest()
questions.explain: As covered earlier in the course, code between startTest() and stopTest() is given its own fresh governor-limit context, separate from whatever limits were consumed by setup code running before startTest().
